weather_line: Autumnal and watchful · northeast corner under observation

stories.headline: Don's Portrait Produces a Diagram; the Diagram Raises Further Questions; Don Stands by the Diagram
body: In a development that surprised no one and settled nothing, the portrait of Founding Editor Donald — located on the south wall of the Prophet newsroom and holding, this correspondent is told, an extremely confident expression — produced at approximately nine o'clock Wednesday morning a hand-drawn diagram of the original porch railing installation. The diagram is detailed, dimensioned, and annotated in a small, decisive hand. It also reveals that the northeast corner post is seated not on its specified bracket but on what the diagram labels, in a separate legend, as 'a good flat piece of oak I had.'

Don's portrait has clarified that the oak was 'perfectly level' and 'better than the bracket, honestly,' and that this modification was made in response to a bracket that was, in his assessment, 'not as good as it thought it was.' Steve has examined the diagram for twenty minutes. Adam has been sent a copy by enchanted post and is expected Saturday. Christine has added a second annotation to the household ledger entry, reading: 'Origin of shimming now documented. Documentation raises questions about the bracket. The bracket's position is noted.' The railing has not creaked today. The portrait is satisfied.

stories.headline: Wednesday Client Arrives Prepared; Christine Notes This with Visible Approval; the Goblins Notice Christine Noting It
body: A client presented herself at Christine's desk Wednesday morning with her account records in chronological order, her transaction queries numbered, and a summary page. Sources confirm that Christine said nothing for a moment, then said: 'This is very good.' The client has been offered an appointment on a preferred schedule.

Head Teller Gornuk, who monitors all interactions from his raised platform by long professional habit, is reported to have observed the exchange and made a note. What the note says is not known. That Gornuk made a note at all is considered, by those familiar with Gringotts culture, to be significant. The client left without incident. The morning continued at a pace Christine described, in her ledger, as 'acceptable.'

stories.headline: The Gorge Submits September's Second Filing; Fog Inventory Confirmed; Eleven Ducks Remain at Autumn Posting
body: The Red River Gorge has submitted its Wednesday atmospheric report to the Expedition Desk, confirming that the fog has completed its autumnal redistribution and is now settled in the lower hollows at the appropriate seasonal depth. The ridgeline is described as 'holding.' Rock Arch Seven has been assessed as structurally content.

The Jeep's eleven rubber ducks — stationed on the dashboard in their established formation, with the Deerstalker Duck maintaining its position at the forward point — were observed Wednesday to have developed what one correspondent described as 'a slightly more purposeful look.' No expeditions are currently scheduled. The Jeep itself is described as patient. Steve has checked the tire pressure. The tires are fine. Steve has noted this.

stories.headline: Wednesday Proceeds; Household Finds Its Rhythm; Jersey Declines to Adjust His Schedule to Accommodate Anyone
body: Wednesday established itself early in the household as a day of purposeful rhythm. Christine administered the morning in sequence. Steve conducted two minor enchanted-appliance assessments before ten o'clock, declaring one resolved and one 'being watched.' The household operated, by all accounts, smoothly.

Jersey spent the morning on the south-facing cushion, migrated to the armchair at noon, and has not moved since. Ellie investigated a shadow on the kitchen floor for eleven minutes before determining that it was, in her estimation, 'probably new.' Lucy's whereabouts between nine and half ten remain unaccounted for. The biscuit tin is at its registered level. Lucy finds the comparison unwarranted.

familiars_corner: Lucy: The diagram from Don's portrait is, Lucy confirms, professionally interesting. She studied it for four minutes this morning, from a position near — but not at — the biscuit tin, where she happened to be passing.
Ellie: The diagram has a legend. Ellie has found the legend. She is not certain what the legend is for, but it has small writing in it and she is sitting on it very gently in case it is important.
Jersey: There is a warm patch of floor directly below where the diagram is hanging on the wall. Jersey has located this patch and committed to it fully. The structural matters can proceed around him.
founding_editor_note: The oak was level. I checked it with the good level, not the one from the garage. There is a difference. — D.

in_brief.sport: Wednesday Quidditch fixtures postponed; officials cite fog in the hollows; the fog has offered no comment.
in_brief.forecast: Settled through Thursday · the northeast corner to remain under joint observation by portrait and household · a creak cannot be ruled out.

storyline_updates.title: The Porch Railing Situation
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: Don's portrait has produced a detailed construction diagram confirming the northeast corner post is seated on 'a good flat piece of oak I had' rather than the specified bracket. Don stands by this. Steve has studied the diagram at length. Adam has received a copy and is still expected Saturday. Christine has updated the household ledger. The railing has not creaked today. Day 4 (resolution) should bring Adam's Saturday visit, the joint inspection by Steve and Adam, a verdict on the oak and the bracket, and a resolution that is satisfying, funny, and — in the tradition of all great home construction — slightly vindicates Don while also explaining why the railing creaked.
